title: Continuous PR gate: synthetic burst & rolling-baseline performance harness
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a lightweight, PR-friendly performance harness that synthesizes short bursts of realistic token traffic and compares results to a rolling baseline to detect p95 and tokens/sec regressions before merge. The harness must be cheap enough to run in presubmit, produce stable statistical signals, and provide clear pass/fail guidance plus links to the full baseline and trace artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: PR-level check runs in under 12 minutes for typical model smoke (<= 1e6 tokens simulated across micro-bursts)
Detects regressions >5% on p95 latency or >8% degradation on tokens/sec with >= 90% recall and controlled false positive rate (<5%) on historical signal set
Results include p95, p50, tokens/sec, variance estimate, and a brief auto-generated note describing the likely regression vector (batching/KV/cache/hot-path)
Baseline storage: rolling baseline retained for last 30 days and accessible via a stable S3 path and dashboard link
Gating behavior: PR fails only when statistical test exceeds threshold OR ops override criteria documented in runbook
steps: Create micro-burst traffic generator that replays sampled request shapes from prod trace slices (prefix lengths, seq len distribution)
Instrument ephemeral infra in PR pipeline: small dedicated GPU job with constrained concurrency and seeded randomness
Compute per-run summary metrics (p50, p95, tokens_per_sec, tokenize_time, kv-hit-rate) and compute Bayesian credible interval for p95
Compare to rolling baseline using sequential hypothesis test with early stopping; produce human-readable delta summary
Push run artifact (raw traces + aggregated metrics) to S3 and post summary to PR with dashboard/trace links
Add circuit-breaker: if ephemeral infra unavailable, skip gate and add informative comment so reviewer can triage
notes: 2025-02-05: Spike completed. Prototype uses 1xT4-equivalent runner and resumed stable p95 within 10% of prod smoke on small sample.
2025-02-12: Decided to use Bayesian sequential testing (beta-binomial for per-token event proxies + student-t for latency) to reduce run-time and control FP rate.
2025-02-19: Trade-off: more conservative thresholds reduce FP but increase missed regressions; chose thresholds tuned to historical regression corpus (see linked doc).

2025-02-27: PM feedback (Dana Li): prefer an explanatory sentence on PR comment highlighting likely root cause (e.g., batching changes vs quantization) — added heuristics mapping metric deltas to vectors.
2025-03-01: Infra note from SRE (Omar Bennett): add auto-retry on transient OOM and mark run as flaky if jitter in tokens/sec > 12% across retries.

2025-03-04: Running end-to-end smoke in staging pipeline; observed one false positive on a PR that changed logging only — plan to add quick fingerprint filter to whitelist non-performance-impacting changes.
links: Historical regression corpus used for tuning: s3://redwood-perf/regression-corpus/2024-q4/
outcome_summary: Mid-March goal: merge a presubmit PR gate that reliably prevents major perf regressions while minimizing developer friction. Initial staging runs show promise; next steps are hardening flaky detection and integrating with the console baseline viewer. Post-merge follow-ups: dashboarding alerts, on-call playbook, and canary-to-prod rollout policy.
